raw_evidence.observed_failure: All four fail while awaiting the first stdout endpoint line. Three use HostHarness wording; one standalone case uses the gRPC endpoint wording. This block contains no syscall unwrap failure.
raw_evidence.distinct_from: This is one representative emitted test block, not a new count of all repeated Bazel attempts or all code-mode targets.

call_chain.finding: Three cases call HostHarness::start("grpc://127.0.0.1:0"). tcp_listener_opens_a_grpc_session independently spawns the same binary and args, then waits 10 seconds for read_line.

cargo_bin("codex-code-mode-host") → argv [--listen, grpc://127.0.0.1:0]; stdin null, stdout/stderr piped, kill_on_drop true. The sole startup readiness observation is a 10-second stdout line wait, then scheme/prefix validation.
Explicit CARGO_BIN_EXE metadata precedes NEXTEST_BIN_EXE; Bazel resolves through runfiles. Missing metadata/path is an error; there is no current_exe or PATH binary fallback.
Current-thread Tokio runtime; tracing writes stderr; Clap parses listen; invokes run_main.
grpc:// parses a SocketAddr and directly invokes grpc_transport::run_tcp_listener. No UDS is used in this route.
TcpListener::bind, local_addr, one INFO log, println!(http://...), and explicit stdout.flush occur before constructing gRPC routes or accepting client requests.
Uses standard codex_rust_crate(name=code-mode-host). Actual Bazel metadata/concurrency is assigned to the CI agent; this review does not infer runtime binary bytes from source declaration.

conclusions: The observed failures precede any HTTP/gRPC request or session-open assertion.
UDS pathname length is outside this representative TCP route.
The Rust path before endpoint publication does not initialize a CodeMode session or issue a provider request. This does not characterize dynamic-loader or pre-main activity.
A missing binary or ordinary exec-format failure should fail at cargo_bin/spawn with a different source error; the observed timeout does not support selecting either as the established cause.

The original child stderr is piped but never consumed or included in timeout errors. The original child status is not reported at the timeout boundary. The raw log cannot distinguish a live blocked child, delayed launch, pre-main activity, or another pre-readiness failure.
Do not infer that raising the 10-second limit, serializing all tests, or changing the listener is a justified fix from this evidence.

minimum_diagnostic_proposal.scope: Test-only startup helper plus the equivalent standalone case; no product listener change.
preserve: Existing endpoint scheme validation and all protocol assertions
Same exact child binary and argv
kill_on_drop for the retained owned child
No retries, fallback, or test skipping
add: Record resolved child program and fixed argv before launch.
Continuously drain child stderr into a bounded diagnostic buffer while readiness is awaited; continue draining/discarding beyond the retained bound to avoid introducing pipe backpressure.
On the existing timeout/EOF/error path, report the original stdout partial state, bounded stderr already observed, and nonblocking try_wait result for this child before it is dropped.
Do not add an unbounded stderr await or a new post-timeout grace period. Any cleanup waits must use remaining time from the same deadline or retain an explicit unknown status.
minimum_diagnostic_proposal.limit: A diagnostic candidate is not implemented or executed here. It can identify the actual failure without changing the success gate.
